why: The student says the file could be called Greeting.java while it still holds public class hello, but Java requires a public class to be saved in a file with the same name, so javac would reject it; this is the ClassNameMatchesFile misconception.

concepts.quote: I can rename the file to Greeting.java and keep public class hello.
concepts.why: It treats the file name and the public class name as independent, but public class hello must be saved in hello.java.
It applies the wrong rule that a public class's name does not have to match its file name.
The answer suggests the renamed file would still work but makes no direct claim about what javac does.
